Multivariate Linear Regression    Definition

Definition



Multiple linear regression is used to estimate the relationship between two or
more independent variables (X1, X2, · · · , Xk) and one dependent variable (Y ).

                     yi = β0 + β1xi1 + β2xi2 + · · · + βkxik + ui

Multivariate Linear Regression    Derivation

Solve the minimization problem





Minimize the following function:

                          n
         L(ˆβ0, ˆβ1, · · · , ˆβk) = X(yi −ˆβ0 −ˆβ1xi1 −ˆβ2xi2 −· · · −ˆβkxik)2
                             i=1


Use the same algebraic method as we used for solving the OLS estimation for the
simple linear regression model.

Multivariate Linear Regression   A ”partialling out” interpretation

Frisch-Waugh-Lowell Theorem



When estimating a model in the following form:

                  y = β0 + β1x1 + β2x2 + · · · + βkxk + u


The following estimators of β1 are equivalent:
    The OLS estimator obtained by regressing y on x1, x2, · · · , xk.
    The OLS estimator obtained by regressing y on ˆr1, where ˆr1 is the estimated
     residual obtained by regressing x1 on x2, · · · , xk.


”Partialling out” interpretation
     βj is the average change in y when xj changes by one unit holding all the
    other covariates constant (the other factors have been partialled out).

Multivariate Linear Regression   MLR. assumptions

MLR.1-MLR.4




MLR.1 (Linear in Parameters)
    y = β0 + β1x1 + β2x2 + · · · + βkxk + u

MLR.2 (Random Sampling)
     (xi1, xi2, · · · , xik, yi) : i = 1, 2, · · · , n are i.i.d

MLR.3 (No Perfect Collinearity)
    rank(Xn×k) = k
      |ρxi,xj| ̸= 1, where i ̸= j.
MLR.4 (Zero Conditional Mean)
     E(ui|xi1, xi2, · · · , xik) = 0

Multivariate Linear Regression   Omitted variable bias

Model specification





True model:
                        y = β0 + β1x1 + β2x2 + u

Full estimation:
                                             ˆy = ˆβ0 + ˆβ1x1 + ˆβ2x2

Omitted estimation:
                                                  ˜y = ˜β0 + ˜β1x1
